course_name_original: English B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 3/3
course_name_en: English B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 3/3
prerequisites: English language proficiency at least at A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Able to use grammatical structures, phraseology and vocabulary allowing to understand texts of a general nature, describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, of an academic and industry nature, and allowing for relatively fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.

Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided that they concern industry issues and current affairs, and can interpret the acquired information.
Able to write understandable informational and argumentative texts on general and industry topics, conduct correspondence typical for the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Able to prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry topics and participate in discussions quite fluently and spontaneously, also in a professional environment.
Able to present clearly their conclusions and opinions on general, academic and professional topics in written and oral form.

syllabus_topics: Grammar: Present Simple tense, Present Continuous tense, Past Simple tense, Past Continuous tense, Present Perfect tense, Present Perfect Continuous tense, Future Simple tense, Past Perfect Simple tense, 'be going to' expression, countable and uncountable nouns, adjectives and adverbs, verb forms – -ing and infinitive, modal verbs, conditional modes I, II, III, subordinate clauses of time, relative clauses, conjunctions, passive voice, reported speech, word formation.

Topics and vocabulary: Introduction and practice in various contexts of vocabulary and phraseology related to the following topics: studies (description of faculty and nature of studies), career plans and job searching, qualifications and character traits, private and professional interests, technological progress and innovations, latest industry achievements, company structure and functioning, regulations and instructions, employee professional development, official duties, finance, describing charts and presenting trends, phenomena and trends in the modern world, multicultural society, ethics at university and in the workplace.

Language functions: introducing oneself, greetings and farewells, receiving guests at university and in a company, conducting conversations at meetings, receptions, conferences, making appointments, phone calls, expressing opinions and suggestions, giving advice, inviting and accepting invitations, expressing offers of help and requests, seeking information, active participation in academic and professional discussions, giving presentations, negotiating, describing using numbers and units of measurement and weight.
Other skills: writing emails, writing letters, preparing descriptions, writing argumentative texts.
assessment_rules: The condition for passing is to receive a positive grade from all colloquia conducted during the semester. In case of a negative grade in the first attempt, the student has the right to improve it, resulting in the negative grade being replaced by a positive one that counts towards the average. Improving a grade obtained in the second attempt results in the average of the two grades being entered; the average partial grade for passing the test cannot be less than 3.0. Unjustified absence from a test results in the loss of that attempt. Each student has the right to two retake colloquia, which can take place at intervals of no less than 2 days. The final grade for the language course is the arithmetic mean of all grades obtained by the student from passing individual semesters and the foreign language exam. The condition for admission to the exam is passing the compulsory language course semesters.
